dedupe_keys.name: fracfocus hydraulic fracturing chemical disclosure registry

description: FracFocus is a public registry of hydraulic fracturing chemical disclosures for oil and gas wells in the United States, growing since 2011 as a one-stop resource for people wishing to explore what is in fracturing fluid; the page notes that most formulas consist of 0.5 to 2 percent chemical additives and 98 to 99 percent water and sand. Each disclosure describes a treated well and its ingredients, and recent additions include water source data and, since March 2025, hydraulic fracturing disclosures for non-oil and gas wells, with a feature on additional well data in March 2026. Coverage is national with well-level records. Access: the site provides a full SQL data download to the public, plus a searchable disclosure interface. Licence and cost: free to download; the page states no licence. Caveats: disclosures are made by operators, and the registry describes stimulation jobs, not well production or condition. It suits environmental exposure and water resource risk studies around oil and gas fields and supply chain analysis of well construction, and relates to the EIA petroleum supply and prices record catalogued here.
